panels.title: Used capacity per volume
panels.description: Capped at 100 series. With thousands of volumes a graph of all of them is neither readable nor cheap to render, so narrow the scope with the variables at the top rather than raising the cap.

targets.expr: topk(100, max by (csi_driver_name, pv_name, cluster_guid, storage_class_name, filesystem_name, volume_type, organization, pvc_name, pvc_namespace, pvc_uid) (last_over_time(weka_csi_volume_used_bytes{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name"}[$value_max_age])))

panels.title: Total capacity per volume

panels.title: Free capacity per volume
panels.description: The volumes with the least free space, which are the ones worth watching. Capped at 100 series. With thousands of volumes a graph of all of them is neither readable nor cheap to render, so narrow the scope with the variables at the top rather than raising the cap.

targets.expr: bottomk(100, max by (csi_driver_name, pv_name, cluster_guid, storage_class_name, filesystem_name, volume_type, organization, pvc_name, pvc_namespace, pvc_uid) (last_over_time(weka_csi_volume_free_bytes{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name"}[$value_max_age])))

panels.title: Utilisation per volume
panels.description: Used as a percentage of each volume's own capacity. Dashed lines mark the 85% and 95% alert thresholds. Capped at 100 series. With thousands of volumes a graph of all of them is neither readable nor cheap to render, so narrow the scope with the variables at the top rather than raising the cap.

targets.expr: topk(100, 100 * max by (csi_driver_name, pv_name, cluster_guid, storage_class_name, filesystem_name, volume_type, organization, pvc_name, pvc_namespace, pvc_uid) (last_over_time(weka_csi_volume_used_bytes{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name"}[$value_max_age])) / clamp_min(max by (csi_driver_name, pv_name, cluster_guid, storage_class_name, filesystem_name, volume_type, organization, pvc_name, pvc_namespace, pvc_uid) (last_over_time(weka_csi_volume_capacity_bytes{organization=~"$organization", filesystem_name=~"$filesystem_name", storage_class_name=~"$storage_class_name", pvc_namespace=~"$pvc_namespace", pv_name=~"$pv_name"}[$value_max_age])), 1))

list.name: value_max_age
list.label: Value max age
list.description: How stale a reading may be and still count. Must be larger than the metrics server's quotaCacheValiditySeconds (chart default 300s): each reading carries the timestamp of its own measurement, so a window at or below the cache validity drops the volumes that have not been re-fetched yet, and the panel appears to lose volumes periodically.

list.name: organization
list.label: Tenant
list.description: WEKA organization the volume belongs to.

list.name: storage_class_name
list.label: Storage class
list.description: StorageClass the volume was provisioned from.

list.name: pv_name
list.label: PersistentVolume
list.description: Optional filter down to individual volumes. Leave on All and rely on the 100-series cap, or pick specific volumes to see every one of them.
